answer: A stake-weighted reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks because every identity must lock a deposit before it can trade, and a mirror audit lets peers compare behavior histories across accounts to spot cloned patterns. A whisper of fake endorsements cannot move the score, since endorsements only count from identities with proven work. An attacker who spawns thousands of cheap accounts still hits the nadir of zero trust, because trust grows only from paid, verified transactions, making each fake identity cost more than it can earn.
